blocks.summary: GPC: inference-time enhancement of frozen diffusion BC policies via an action-conditioned predictive world model and lightweight online planning (rank + refine).
BC looks back and is brittle at deployment; MPC looks ahead but is hard to integrate with generative policies; motivating question of test-time adaptability without retraining.

Contribution: three components (generative policy training, predictive world modeling with random exploration, online planning GPC-RANK/GPC-OPT); novelty vs imagined-rollout planners: image-space diffusion world model, frozen-noise inference, unified rank+refine, VLM reward surrogates.
Fig. 1 framework overview: (a) GPC-RANK evaluates multiple proposals in imagination; (b) GPC-OPT refines a single proposal by gradients through the world model.

Generative modeling for robotics (policies, data, dynamics, planning); visual world modeling lineage (IRIS, Dreamer-v3, TDMPC-2, latent-space MPC); GPC differs by explicit image-space action-conditioned video world model used at inference time.
Formalization of I_t, action chunks a_{t:t+T}; generative policy training with Diffusion Policy (H=2, T=16, action horizon 9, DDPM, ResNet18+UNet, 300 epochs AdamW 1e-4/1e-6, 100 denoising steps).

Predictive world modeling: expert pairs plus random-exploration dataset (system identification / sufficient excitation); combined D^W trains W(.); reward model R as trained predictor or VLM surrogate.
GPC-RANK: Eq. (1) sample K proposals, Eq. (2) argmax of R(W(I_t, a^{(k)})); advantages: parallelizable, no hyperparameter tuning, supports non-differentiable and VLM rewards.

GPC-OPT: Eq. (3) reward maximization, Eq. (4) gradient ascent from diffusion-policy warm start with step sizes eta^(l), Eq. (5) final chunk; single shooting analogy; M sequential world-model evaluations.
GPC-RANK+OPT: multi-initialization solving of (3), K x M world-model evaluations; Alg. 1 summary; modern diffusion models enable near physics-accurate visual prediction.
Algorithm 1 pseudocode unifying GPC-RANK (M=0) and GPC-OPT (K=1, M>0).

MLP for state-based dynamics; visual world model as recursive single-step conditional diffusion predictor: Eq. (6) o_{t+1}=f_vision(o_{t-H:t}, a_t), Eq. (7) denoising iteration with denoiser D_phi (architecture of [42]).
Fig. 2 architecture: recursive single-step predictors (left), UNet denoiser conditioned on history and action for N_d steps (right). Crop includes stray body text from the right column of page 4.

Two-phase training (single-step supervision, then recursive T-step joint supervision), H=4, N_d=3, EDM-based diffusion; Remark 1 freeze-the-noise: fix o^{N_d}_{t+1}=0 at inference, otherwise GPC-OPT fails.
Evaluation plan: state-based pushing, four vision-based simulation tasks, two real-world tasks; ablations on K, M and inference-time baselines.

State-based Push-T setup, MLP world model, registration-loss reward (l2 distance over transformed object vertices); all GPC variants beat BC; best variant 0.934 approaches GT-simulator planning 0.952.
Table I transcribed to Markdown: BC 0.812; GPC-RANK 0.898/0.932/0.934 (K=100/1000/5000); GPC-OPT 0.886; GPC-RANK+OPT 0.912/0.914/0.891; GT simulator 0.952. IoU over 100 seeds.

Four vision tasks; diffusion world model quality: SSIM vs deep visual foresight and AVDC; baseline footnote URLs (github Xiaohui9607/physical_interaction_video_prediction_pytorch, flow-diffusion/AVDC) kept in source_map only.
Fig. 3 predicted rollouts on four tasks with per-task SSIM 0.971/0.973/0.961/0.950 over ~250 frames, 5 seeds.
Fig. 4 world-model comparison: GT 1.000, Ours 0.983, Deep Visual Foresight 0.943, AVDC 0.955 (SSIM, 10 sampled predictions, 100 samples). Crop top contaminated by Fig. 3 / Table II caption text.

Reward strategies: differentiable ResNet18+MLP predictor, or zero-shot VLM (ChatGPT-4o, final frames at resolution 96, fixed prompt, temperature 0.2, one query per decision step); planning performance vs LaDi-WM, V-GPS, DreamerV3 with shared policy/data and 100 candidates.
Table II transcribed to Markdown: GPC-RANK best on all four tasks (0.739, 0.767(0.761), 0.989(0.973), 0.730); scores over 50 seeds.
Table III transcribed to Markdown: score/timing trade-off, BC 0.642/0.457s to GPC-RANK+OPT 0.882/374.102s; baseline printed as (K=1, M=1) in source.
Ablations: GPC-RANK ~10%, GPC-OPT ~15%, GPC-RANK+OPT up to ~25% over BC; planning-only MPPI/CEM/gradient-ascent below 0.2; random exploration adds ~10%; summary of complementary benefits.
Fig. 5 bar chart: with vs without random exploration for GPC-RANK and GPC-OPT (about +10%).
Real Push-T (ResNet+MLP reward from AprilTag-derived registration loss) and clothes folding (progressing reward); 10 trials per task; policy and world model fully vision-based at inference.
Fig. 6 real Push-T trajectories: baseline vs GPC-RANK (K=10) vs GPC-OPT (printed K=0, M=25; likely K=1).
Fig. 7 real clothes-folding trajectories: baseline vs GPC-RANK (K=10).
Fig. 8 real-world success rates over 10 trials: Push-T 0.5/0.7/0.7 (baseline/RANK/OPT), clothes 0.3/0.7 (baseline/RANK), values read from chart.
GPC enables robust test-time adaptation without retraining by combining diffusion priors, action-conditioned visual world models, and flexible rewards.
Inference cost dominated by diffusion world-model rollouts (~90-95% of runtime; ~3 s per decision cycle for real-world GPC-RANK); future: distillation, faster solvers, hardware acceleration.
44 entries; not translated line by line per reader contract; lineages summarized bilingually in paper.md.
Dataset sizes: Push-T 500 expert + 6x500 perturbations + 7 long-horizon; Triangle Drawing 30/100; Block Stacking 50/100; Cube & Sphere 100/100; real-world 100 demos + 5 random-play videos per task.
